prompt.context: Your client is FlashPro Inc., a San Francisco based technology company that develops and sells wearable and mountable action cameras. FlashPro's CEO believes that the company's growth has stagnated and has hired your firm to remedy that issue.
prompt.question: FlashPro's growth has stagnated. How would you approach diagnosing the problem and identifying growth opportunities?

clarifying_info.q: Is the company public or private?
Where does FlashPro sell its products?
clarifying_info.a: It sells its products in the US and internationally.
Their main product is CamPro, a mounted camera mainly used when playing action sports. It has also recently started being used in other recreational activities.

clarifying_info.q: Does FlashPro manufacture its own products?
clarifying_info.a: No, FlashPro does not manufacture its products — it contracts with manufacturers in China.

clarifying_info.q: How does FlashPro sell its products?
clarifying_info.a: FlashPro sells through 3 channels: Distributors, Retail, and FlashPro's Website.

clarifying_info.q: What is the competitive environment like?
clarifying_info.a: The industry is highly competitive and customers are very loyal to each brand.
Gross margin has remained steady at 50%.

clarifying_info.q: What is the US vs. international revenue split?
clarifying_info.a: Over the last 5 years, 60% of camera sales have come from the US. The split is expected to be similar in 2018.

exhibits.title: Action Camera Potential Market in the US
exhibits.shows: A bar chart showing the US action camera addressable market (potential customers) from 2014 to 2020, with actuals through 2017 and estimates for 2018-2020.

exhibits.title: Action Camera Market Penetration in the US
exhibits.shows: A bar chart showing the percentage of the potential market that has already purchased an action camera, from 2014 to 2020 (actuals through 2017, estimates for 2018-2020).

exhibits.title: 2016 Action Camera Market Share Distribution
exhibits.shows: A pie chart showing each player's share of the action camera market. The note states market share distribution is the same in the US and worldwide and has remained steady for the last 5 years, and that FlashPro is the only company offering wearables.

exhibits.title: International Market Entry Options
exhibits.shows: A table comparing four potential expansion countries — Argentina, Japan, Australia, and Sweden — across current camera market size, FlashPro's expected Year 1 market share, expected annual growth over 3 years, and sales channel distribution (Distributors / Retail / FlashPro's Website). All dollar amounts are in thousands.

data.note: After Year 3, the expected market annual growth for all countries is 5%. Dollar amounts in thousands.

framework: Market analysis: Competitors, customers, substitutes, and suppliers (e.g., competitive dynamics, customer loyalty, FlashPro's unique wearable positioning)
Profitability tree: Break revenue into volume (market size x penetration x market share) and price; break costs into COGS, R&D, G&A, and Sales & Marketing
Growth levers: Marketing mix (4Ps — product attributes, sales channels, price, advertising); new markets (product line expansion, new geographies); organic vs. inorganic (M&A)

questions.prompt: Question 1: Using Exhibits 1, 2, and 3, what is FlashPro's expected Gross Profit for 2018? (All amounts in thousands; camera price = $250; COGS = 50% of sales; US = 60% of total sales)
questions.guidance: Candidate should build up from US addressable market to US revenue, then scale to international, then apply gross margin. Strong candidates will call out the distinction between addressable market size, penetration rate, and market share.

math.setup: US Camera Sales = Addressable Market x Penetration Rate x FlashPro Market Share x Price. International Sales scaled by US/International split. Gross Profit = Total Revenue x (1 - COGS%).
steps: US Camera Sales = 16,000 (thousands) x 85% x 30% x $250 = $1,020,000 (thousands)

questions.prompt: Question 2: What are FlashPro's revenue growth prospects keeping everything constant, and what other alternatives could help boost the top line?
questions.guidance: A good candidate draws key insights from Exhibits 1-3: the US market is maturing (penetration rising toward 95% by 2020, market size growth slowing), and FlashPro's 30% market share has been stable — organic US growth is limited and fierce competition makes share gains difficult. Candidate should then structure growth levers: (1) Marketing Mix / 4Ps: product attributes (expand wearables), new/better sales channels, pricing strategies, advertising; (2) New Markets: product line expansion, new geographies; (3) Organic development vs. Inorganic (M&A/partnerships). Excellent candidates will note that market saturation in the US points strongly toward geographic expansion.

questions.prompt: Question 3 (with Exhibit 4): From an economic perspective, which country is the most attractive for FlashPro to enter, and what factors should it consider before entering?
questions.guidance: Candidate should calculate Year 3 revenue for each country: Year 3 Revenue = Current Market Size x Year-1 Market Share x (1 + Annual Growth)^3. The best option is Argentina ($1,165K) — highest Year 3 revenue and a favorable sales channel mix (50% website, which carries higher margins due to no intermediary vs. distributor/retail). An excellent candidate will note that Argentina's high website channel share implies higher margins than Japan or Sweden (which are 10% website / 90% distributor+retail). Pre-entry considerations should be structured: customer habits and brand awareness, local competition, regulation and trade barriers, macroeconomic and geopolitical risk (especially relevant for Argentina), logistics and supply chain, and partnership/distribution strategy.

math.setup: Year 3 Revenue = Current Market Size x Expected Year-1 Market Share x (1 + Annual Growth)^3. Note: compound growth applied to total market; FlashPro's share assumed constant after Year 1.
math.answer: Argentina has the highest Year 3 revenue at ~$1,165 thousand, followed by Japan ($1,013K), Sweden ($951K), and Australia ($932K).

brainstorming.prompt: What alternatives could help FlashPro boost its top line?

categories.name: Marketing Mix (4Ps)
ideas: Improve product attributes: expand wearable line, add new features or accessories
Optimize sales channels: shift mix toward higher-margin website channel, add new retail partners
Adjust pricing: premium tiers for new product lines, bundles
Increase advertising and brand-building to reinforce loyalty in existing markets

categories.name: New Markets — Geographies
ideas: Enter high-growth international markets (e.g., Argentina, Australia, Sweden, Japan)
Target emerging markets with rising outdoor sports participation

categories.name: New Markets — Product/Segment
ideas: Expand into adjacent use cases: drones, dash cams, body cameras for professional/enterprise use
Develop accessories and software/subscription revenue streams
Target new customer segments beyond action sports (travel, vlogging, professional filming)

categories.name: Inorganic Growth
ideas: Acquire a competitor or complementary technology company
Partner with distributors or retailers to accelerate geographic rollout
License technology or brand to expand reach with lower capital outlay

recommendation: Given the maturing US market and fierce competition limiting organic share gains, FlashPro should pursue a geographic expansion strategy to achieve growth

Argentina is the most attractive initial entry market: it offers the highest Year 3 revenue (~$1,165K), a higher expected Year 1 market share (35%), and a sales channel mix weighted 50% toward FlashPro's own website — implying higher margins than alternatives dominated by distributors and retail
risks: Analysis does not account for costs of market entry (marketing, logistics, regulatory compliance, working capital) or competitive responses from local or global players
Year 1 market share assumptions (especially Argentina at 35%) may be aggressive for a brand with limited local presence; actual ramp could be slower
next_steps: Conduct detailed due diligence on the Argentinian market: customer habits, brand awareness, local competitors, regulatory environment, and macroeconomic/geopolitical conditions
Assess FlashPro's internal capabilities (supply chain, customer support, language/localization) needed to support international expansion
Develop a go-to-market plan covering advertising, channel partnerships, promotional pricing, and a phased product launch strategy for Argentina
